answer: Concrete mechanism: per-identity sequential proof of work. Each epoch an identity publishes a hash chain that cannot be parallelized, so one machine yields only a couple of identities while peer verification stays cheap. Forging N identities costs N machines busy for the whole epoch: a real power and hardware bill that scales with the attack and earns nothing back, since standing accrues only from attested work. Difficulty retargets as hardware cheapens, so a willow of burner accounts gains no bridge to standing, and the cedar of a proven history cannot be mass-farmed.
